prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: worried the house is in a flood zone. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 4)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member says they are worried the house is in a flood zone, check whether the concern is about river, surface water or coastal flooding, as the next steps and urgency can differ even if the address itself is the same."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the property sits near a named watercourse, I treat recent heavy rain and any local warning from the Met Office as useful context, but I still need evidence of actual ingress, standing water or damage before escalating beyond triage."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the concern is only based on a map, I prefer to ask for a clear photo of the location and any visible flood markers rather than over-reassuring or over-escalating too early."},{"type":"observation","content":"When members are anxious about flood risk, they often need a calm explanation of what is covered now versus what would matter if water had actually entered the home, so I keep the questions plain and practical."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there has been no flooding, no nearby overtopping and no internal damage, a claim usually stays as an enquiry for advice rather than a loss event, which helps avoid unnecessary referrals and delays."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member mentions recent blocked drains, road surface water or garden ponding, I flag those details because they can point to surface water exposure even if the house is not in a recognised flood area."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the property is in a low-lying area or close to a river, I prefer to ask whether the member has taken any temporary protection steps, such as moving valuables upstairs, because that helps judge immediate risk and sensible guidance."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the member reports no current damage but says flood water has been close before, I note the history carefully, as past near misses can be relevant for future triage even if the present claim is not covered by a flood loss."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the concern is about a mortgage or sale rather than damage, I separate the insurance question from the property-value worry, because members often need different signposting for each."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the flood concern is vague, I ask three quick things in order: where the water is coming from, whether it has entered the building, and whether anything is still changing, because that gives me the fastest route to the right decision."}]}
